card.name: Words before toxicology study types
card.fires_on: The word or word part just before "study" or "studies" in nonclinical toxicology text, such as two-year, gene mutation, reproduction, or chromosomal aberrations.

modes.label: Study duration or design
modes.description: The hyphenated part after "two" that describes a study's length or design.
modes.example: In a two<<-generation>> fertility study in which clonazepam

modes.label: Genetic toxicity terms
modes.description: Words about mutation or chromosome damage in lab assays.
modes.example: Fifteen separate in vitro gene<< mutation>> studies with malathion of unknown purity

modes.label: Reproduction terms
modes.description: Reproduction or development words that come before studies or toxicants.
modes.example: In<< reproduction>> studies, no effects on fertility were found

card.writes: It adds a push toward harm and damage words, such as "harm", but the effect is weak.
card.plain: It marks the spot in animal-study sections where a word names the kind of safety study, such as mutation, reproduction, or two-year studies.
